nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: The primary method introduced is Nearest Neighbor Normativity (N3), a novel framework using local density estimation based on the Nearest Neighbor Algorithm. For comparison purposes, they also used Bayesian Linear Regression (BLR) via the Predictive Clinical Neuroscience toolkit to derive traditional normative modeling z-scores.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: We introduce Nearest Neighbor Normativity (N3), a novel framework designed to resolve the confound between natural diversity and subtle pathological patterns. It evaluates individual brain structures from several meaningful viewpoints, accommodates a variety of co-existing normative prototypes and accounts for individually varying progression rates of brain structural decline.; The N3 approach is based on local density estimation in tailored control groups. To establish a normative reference for the local density seen in a representative sample, we here use the simple and intuitive Nearest-Neighbor algorithm.; We calculate normative models on the training data using the Predictive Clinical Neuroscience toolkit as described in Rutherford et al. [22]. To train the models, we normalize GM, WM, WMH, CSF by Total Intracranial Volume (TIV) and fit Bayesian Linear Regression models with default parameters.

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: The study uses five global brain structural volumes as response variables: gray matter volume (GM), white matter volume (WM), white matter hyperintensity volume (WMH), cerebrospinal fluid volume (CSF), and total intracranial volume (TIV). These measures were extracted from T1-weighted MRI scans preprocessed using CAT12.
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: Our analysis focuses on gray matter (GM), white matter (WM), hyperintense white matter (WMH), total intracranial volume (TIV) and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) volumes. These global measures provide a comprehensive overview of brain structure.; In our application to brain structure, we stratify the training sample by sex and age, resulting into 100 control groups containing same-aged females or males (22 to 72 years), respectively. Each sample is characterized by 5 different features, namely the brain structural volumes (GM, WM, WMH, CSF, TIV) of each individual.

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: The N3 framework stratifies the training sample by sex and age to create demographically matched control groups. Age is used to define control groups along the aging continuum (22 to 72 years), and sex is used to separate males and females into distinct control groups. The traditional normative models (BLR) also normalize features by Total Intracranial Volume (TIV).
